title: Mouse Without Boarders won't move to other machine while Full Screen Windowed Application is running
author: wrmarinelli

judgment.rationale: The issue identifies the fullscreen-windowed mode, the affected games, and the failed transition between two Mouse Without Borders machines. A diagnostic ZIP is attached. The report is sufficient for a maintainer to reproduce, but does not identify whether the game captures the cursor or MWB misses the boundary transition.
evidence: The reporter says MWB previously allowed cursor and keyboard transfer while a fullscreen-windowed game was focused.
The current failure is that the pointer cannot move to the secondary PC while Final Fantasy XIV or Star Trek Online is focused.
The issue includes a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP and identifies PowerToys 0.111.2 on Windows 11 Pro.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with a paired MWB setup and compare the fullscreen-windowed game path with a normal window before selecting a cursor-boundary fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: No fix attempt is linked. A low-confidence hypothesis is that the fullscreen-windowed game's cursor/focus behavior prevents Mouse Without Borders from completing its screen-edge handoff.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Mouse Without Borders screen-edge handoff with fullscreen-windowed apps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A fullscreen-windowed application may capture or confine the primary PC's cursor, or otherwise alter focus so Mouse Without Borders does not process the boundary crossing; the report does not establish which behavior occurs.
plan: Reproduce the failure with the named game in fullscreen-windowed mode and compare it with the same game windowed and with a normal foreground application.
Trace the Mouse Without Borders cursor-boundary and focus/input-sharing path while the game is active to determine whether the cursor is confined or the handoff event is missed.
If MWB suppresses a valid boundary transition, adjust that path without disrupting intentional game cursor confinement and add regression coverage for fullscreen-windowed and ordinary windows.
verification: On a paired Mouse Without Borders setup, move the cursor from the primary PC to the secondary PC with Final Fantasy XIV or Star Trek Online focused in fullscreen-windowed mode.
Verify the same handoff in ordinary windowed mode and confirm that keyboard/mouse control returns correctly after moving back.

confidence.rationale: The failure mode is concrete, but no cursor trace or controlled comparison distinguishes game cursor capture from an MWB boundary/focus regression.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders stops transferring the pointer to a paired PC while a fullscreen-windowed game is focused, although the reporter says the same workflow previously worked.
known_information: The reporter identifies PowerToys 0.111.2, Windows 11 Pro, and Final Fantasy XIV and Star Trek Online as affected applications.
The stated mode is fullscreen-windowed, not fullscreen-exclusive.
A PowerToys diagnostic ZIP is attached; there are no issue comments.
The reported 0.111.2 version is retained as unverified reporter text, not accepted as a known release.
inferences: The game may be capturing or confining the pointer, or MWB may miss a screen-edge transition while the game owns focus.
The report does not yet distinguish an application-specific cursor behavior from a regression in Mouse Without Borders.
issue_context.analysis: The report supplies a concrete, maintainer-reproducible scenario and a diagnostic archive, so another generic request for logs is unnecessary. Reproduce the cursor handoff and compare game/window modes before choosing a code change.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue report and its diagnostic ZIP link; no comments or linked duplicate/fix are present.

The owning implementation is Mouse Without Borders under src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App, particularly its Core and Service areas; no current evidence pinpoints the failing cursor or focus branch.
Revalidated the full report and #51077 grouping: fullscreen-windowed Final Fantasy XIV/Star Trek Online blocks transfer, normal-window behavior is the control; the grouping is not a covering fix.

actions.label: Reproduce fullscreen-windowed MWB handoff
actions.note: Use the affected game's reported window mode and compare it with a normal foreground window.

reproduce.title: Test Mouse Without Borders cursor handoff during a game
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.111.2 on Windows 11 Pro, as reported
prerequisites: Two Windows PCs connected and configured in Mouse Without Borders.
Final Fantasy XIV or Star Trek Online running on the primary PC in fullscreen-windowed mode; do not use fullscreen-exclusive mode.
steps: With the game focused, move the pointer toward the configured screen edge leading to the secondary PC.
Observe whether the pointer and keyboard control transfer to the secondary PC.
Repeat with the game in ordinary windowed mode and with a normal application focused.
If available, compare the attached PowerToys report with the time of each attempted handoff.
reproduce.expected_result: The pointer crosses to the secondary PC and MWB transfers keyboard/mouse control as it does with a normal foreground application.
reproduce.actual_to_confirm: Whether the game confines the pointer or the MWB edge/focus path fails to initiate the handoff.

status.label: Reproduce fullscreen MWB handoff
status.detail: The game and window mode are identified; a controlled comparison will distinguish cursor capture from an MWB handoff failure.

next_action.label: Reproduce fullscreen-windowed MWB handoff
next_action.reason: Compare the named game modes and ordinary-window handoff before selecting a fix.
